Why simulate

What a simulator gives you, and what it leaves out

What you get

No robot: test code at home on a laptop.

No risk: a wrong sign can’t hit anything.

No waiting for the mechanical team to finish.

Rough physics: close enough to learn from.

What it leaves out

Carpet: the wheels never slip.

Wear: gearboxes and belts stay perfect.

Battery sag: our simulated battery stays at 12 V.

Walls: the robot drives straight through them.

Step 1: the model

A physics model of the KitBot

DriveSim.java

  private final DifferentialDrivetrainSim sim =

      DifferentialDrivetrainSim.createKitbotSim(

1         KitbotMotor.kDualCIMPerSide, KitbotGearing.k8p45,

1         KitbotWheelSize.kSixInch, null);

   

2 private final StructPublisher<Pose2d> posePublisher =

2     NetworkTableInstance.getDefault()

2         .getStructTopic("SimPose", Pose2d.struct).publish();

   

  public void step(double leftVolts, double rightVolts) {

3   sim.setInputs(leftVolts, rightVolts);

3   sim.update(LOOP_SECONDS);

4   posePublisher.set(sim.getPose());

  }

1

Match the real KitBot

2 CIMs per side, 8.45:1 gearing, 6 inch wheels.

2

Publish the pose

NetworkTables carries it to AdvantageScope.

3

Step time forward

Give it volts, then move ahead 20 ms.

4

Share the result

Each step sends the new pose.

Save each output on its way to the motors

CANDriveSubsystem.java

  // The last outputs we commanded, saved for the simulator.

1 private double leftOutput = 0.0;

1 private double rightOutput = 0.0;

   

  private final DifferentialDrive drive =

2     new DifferentialDrive(this::setLeft, this::setRight);

   

  private void setLeft(double output) {

    leftOutput = output;

3   leftLeader.set(output);

  }

   

  private void setRight(double output) {

    rightOutput = output;

3   rightLeader.set(output);

  }

1

Our own copy

A SPARK’s applied output needs extra REV code to update in sim.

2

Methods, not motors

DifferentialDrive calls these with each output.

3

The robot is unchanged

6

Step 3: the sim loop

Step the model in simulationPeriodic()

CANDriveSubsystem.java

  // Built only in simulation. On a real robot this stays null.

1 private final DriveSim sim =

1     RobotBase.isSimulation() ? new DriveSim() : null;

   

2 @Override

2 public void simulationPeriodic() {

3   double leftVolts = leftOutput * NOMINAL_VOLTS;

3   double rightVolts = rightOutput * NOMINAL_VOLTS;

   

    // Real motors stop when disabled. Saved outputs do not.

4   if (DriverStation.isDisabled()) {

      leftVolts = 0.0;

      rightVolts = 0.0;

    }

    sim.step(leftVolts, rightVolts);

  }

1

Sim only

On the roboRIO this stays null.

2

Called for you

The scheduler runs it every loop, only in sim.

3

Output to volts

Deck 2 set 12 V compensation, so 0.5 means 6 V.

4

Stop when disabled

Without this, the robot keeps driving after you disable it.

10

Common mistake

The robot ignores you

What you see

You press keys or move the stick, and the robot sits still.

Why it happens

Robot State isn’t on Teleoperated, Joystick[0] is empty, or another window has keyboard focus.

The fix

Click Teleoperated. Drag your device onto Joystick[0]. Click the Sim GUI window before you use the keys.

Deck 4 · Sim in AdvantageScope

11

Common mistake

The robot drives the wrong way

What you see

You push forward and the robot backs up, spins, or crosses the screen the wrong way.

Why it happens

Backs up: a stick isn’t negated. Spins: one side has a flipped sign. Wrong way on screen: check the view first, because heading 0 faces the red wall.

The fix

Negate both sticks in RobotContainer. Pass both saved outputs to setInputs with no minus signs.

Deck 4 · Sim in AdvantageScope

12

Common mistake

AdvantageScope shows nothing

What you see

The simulator is running, but the field is empty or the title bar says “Searching”.

Why it happens

“Searching” means it hasn’t found the simulator. An empty field means the tab hasn’t been told what to draw.

The fix

Use Connect to Simulator, not Connect to Robot. Then drag SimPose onto Poses.

Deck 4 · Sim in AdvantageScope

13

Best practice

Keep sim code out of the real robot’s path

Keep sim code in simulationPeriodic() and DriveSim. Drive the same commands in sim and on the robot.

Your commands never ask whether they are in a simulator, so what you test is what runs on the robot. Code that never runs on the roboRIO can’t break it at an event.

1.

Drive a figure-8. Then time one full-stick trip across the field.

2.

In DriveSim, change k8p45 to k5p95 or k12p75. Time the same trip.

Recap

What this deck covered

A simulator tests your logic and rough physics, not carpet, wear or battery sag.

DriveSim turns saved outputs into a pose every 20 ms.

simulationPeriodic() runs only in simulation, so the robot path stays clean.

AdvantageScope draws SimPose on the 2D Field tab.
